properties.description: The manifest is derived and the derivation never rewrites history (crates/reflow2-core/tests/write_side.rs) — 8 cases. Every Artifact and Component enters the manifest with its checksum frozen; looking writes nothing (the release_report is still empty after a non-applying call); a re-run adds nothing and, after the live baseline has MOVED, still reports what shipped; an artifact with no checksum still ships and is named in without_checksum; an exclusion that names nothing is refused with the whole call written back out; an exclusion that names something comes back by name rather than by omission; an unknown release is refused; and the end-to-end payoff — one call clears the unreleased_component gap that a partial hand-typed manifest leaves open.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each failing exactly the one test that names it and nothing else: force apply always-true and only the looking-is-not-writing case fails; drop the exclude validation and only the typo'd-exclusion case fails; drop the already-present guard and only the frozen-checksum case fails — which is what proves the guard is doing work rather than the test passing for free. PROVEN ON THE REAL SURFACE: driven over stdio JSON-RPC against the built binary on a copy of reflow2's own 1200-node design, one call produced 160 INCLUDES edges covering all 104 capabilities, the re-run added 0, and the typo'd exclusion came back as "Node not found: Artifact or Component art:nope". It also independently surfaced art:detect as the one artifact with no baseline — the same hole a full reconcile_artifacts sweep found the same hour by a different route.
properties.name: The manifest is derived, and the derivation never rewrites history
